Data-source overview  
The paper proposes a Safe Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for dynamic pedestrian avoidance that equips an autonomous agent with epistemic-uncertainty estimates (via a bootstrapped LSTM ensemble with Monte-Carlo Dropout). The predictive variance is fed into a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) during both training and deployment so that the agent (1) explores efficiently, (2) recognises novel observations, and (3) behaves cautiously, leading to fewer collisions than an uncertainty-unaware baseline.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]  
I am highly confident that every causal-interventional pathway appearing in the paper has been captured, that all nodes are connected, and that JSON formatting is correct (manually double-checked). Remaining uncertainty comes from edge-type subjectivity and the limited maturity information disclosed.

Instruction-set improvement  
The current instructions are meticulous; two refinements would help:  
1. Add an explicit example that shows the acceptable directionality for an edge whose semantic label (e.g. “caused_by”) runs opposite to the arrow required by the path ordering.  
2. Provide a short canonical list of recommended concept-category labels (mechanism, requirement, finding …) to encourage terminological consistency across 500 k sources.

Inference strategy justification  
Moderate inference (confidence 2) was used only when the paper implicitly linked concepts (e.g. connecting the high-level risk to exploration hindrance). All interventions, findings and mechanisms are explicitly described in the source.

Extraction completeness explanation  
16 concept nodes and 4 intervention nodes (≈1 per 300 words) cover every distinct risk→method→finding→intervention element discussed, including training-phase issues (local minima) and implementation feasibility. All nodes appear in at least one path and edges interlink the whole graph.

Key limitations  
• The paper offers only simulation evidence, so intervention-maturity assessments may change with real-world trials.  
• “Environment uncertainty” avenues mentioned in Related Work are out of scope and therefore excluded.
